items.caption: This oracle-script form of 八 consists of two strokes that diverge downward. Oracle-bone inscriptions already use 八 as a numeral, while its proposed connection with separation remains disputed.
items.alt: Two curved strokes diverging downward, with the right stroke taller than the left.
items.selection_reason: The image shows a clear early form, and its specific specimen record makes it useful for illustrating the graph without treating its shape as proof of origin.

items.caption: This Warring States bronze-script form also has two diverging strokes, with the left stroke curving more strongly outward. Its shape can be compared with the oracle-script form, but does not resolve the graph's origin.
items.alt: Two curved strokes opening downward and outward, with the left stroke extending lower than the right.
items.selection_reason: This clearly legible bronze-script example adds a useful graphic comparison; it is a modern redraw sourced to a specific vessel.

limitations.text: The two forms are modern vector redraws rather than photographs of inscribed objects. Their shapes do not establish what the graph originally represented or whether the proposed separation sense preceded its attested numeral use.
